title: Maritime intelligence startup Quartermaster raises another $140M
slides: Quartermaster just raised $140M again—why the hurry?
Maritime intelligence is a high-stakes, fragmented market.
Investors see AI as a way to dominate it.
Your shipping costs may soon be set by algorithms.
Ask: who controls the data that moves your goods?
thread_text:
1. Big Money Moves In

A maritime AI firm just raised $140M in a hurry—and it's not the only one. The rush to automate shipping decisions is already rewriting who gets to set prices.

2. A Fragmented Sea

Maritime intelligence is scattered across brokers, ports, and carriers. No single player sees the whole board, which is exactly why AI firms are buying their way in.

3. Algorithms Set Prices

Your shipping costs may soon be calculated by a model you've never seen. The companies training those models are the same ones now flush with investor cash.

4. Who Owns The Data?

The real battle isn't over boats—it's over the data that moves your goods. Whoever controls that pipeline controls the terms of trade.

5. Check Your Supply Chain

Ask your logistics provider: who owns the data from your shipments? If they can't answer clearly, you're already behind.
